section_summary.extract_value: This section outlines the research objectives and hypotheses for a study examining the interaction between self-compassion and interactions with body-focused others in predicting adaptive (intuitive eating, body appreciation) and maladaptive (body image concerns, negative affect) outcomes. The study employs a within-persons design with nightly ratings over seven days and a between-persons design aggregating data across the week. The hypotheses predict that frequent interactions with body-focused others will negatively impact outcomes only when women are less self-compassionate than usual, with potential buffering effects of higher self-compassion.
